# Security Assessment Service for Code Generated by Open-Weight LLMs

Diploma project, Software Engineering, group SE-2408.

A web service that sends coding tasks to several open-weight LLMs, scans the generated code with
static security analysers, maps the findings to CWE, and reports which model produces more
insecure code and under which prompt conditions.

## Problem, users, outcomes

- **Problem.** LLMs regularly generate vulnerable code, and teams that run open-weight models
  locally have no ready tool to compare models by the security of their output.
- **Target users.** Development and DevSecOps teams choosing a model for internal use, security
  engineers, researchers and instructors.
- **Expected outcomes.** A working service with an API and a web UI; a per-model report
  (share of insecure outputs, CWE distribution, model ranking); a reproducible evaluation method.

Details: [docs/project-proposal.md](docs/project-proposal.md).

## Scope and status

Pre-defense 1 (24 October 2026): analysis and design are done, no running service yet.
The scope and non-goals are in the proposal. Early pipeline experiments live in the course
research project (pilot with Bandit on 15 Python tasks), summarised in
[docs/pilot-results.md](docs/pilot-results.md).

## Technologies (proposed)

Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, vLLM / Ollama, Bandit, Semgrep, CodeQL, Docker,
a web UI framework (open decision). Justification: [docs/technology-comparison.md](docs/technology-comparison.md).
